title: Whether he is a show drummer
summary: The interviewer calls him a showy drummer; he says it is natural feeling, and describes playing head jobs with qualified players.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you some questions about just drumming in general. I've seen you play, what you call yourself, I call it a show drummer at a time. Do you know what that is?
I don't know when you say that it's a show drum.
Like showy when you play. I don't know, just my expressions.
Okay. I would say it's just a natural, I don't know how I look, but hey, I can only play like Jim.

You know your big expressions when you play. Okay, I'm happy to look at that. I know what happened. You know what I always think is a show drummer, Buddy Rich is a show drummer. Yeah, yeah. See how Buddy used to play?
Yeah, maybe that's my movement, you know.
Maybe I knew it's just you.

Yeah, it's a feeling, I don't know. It's how I'm feeling at the particular time, you know. I try to surround myself with some of the better players, you know, make it come out. I've never had any problems. I've always gotten along with different people that I play with, and everybody plays different. You try to be able to capture what's around you, you know, whatever group or whoever the you're playing with, you're playing with at the time. Yeah. And a lot of times it's like really unroiced because the guys know what to do. Like we play at the festival, and I used Julius Schroenberg on bass, he asked me when we start. You know, because everybody's qualified, they know the tunes, you know. If I have a group that we want to be together, we'll be rehearsed like that, but these particular jobs are all head jobs, you call this right off the top, you know. You have a set of tunes you're going to play. And the people are all qualified who you add. So like I said, so many, I respect all the drummers. I respect all the music.
